GameProfile.GameNameInternal: Initial D: Arcade Stage 6 Double Ace

FieldInformation.Hint: Fixed at 60 fps for Initial D network play: always online, and in LAN / offline play once the new LAN mode is on (the online server switches it on step by step). Until then, and with the old LAN-pair settings, this setting still applies. Initial D 6 version 1.2 (TeknoParrot Online included) always uses this setting.

Window size (fullscreen: the display mode). 1360 x 768 is the arcade resolution. Above it the game keeps running at 1360x768 and TeknoParrot scales the whole picture (ResolutionMode Upscale), so every menu, story talk box, ticker and HUD element stays in place. Any size up to 3840 x 2160 (4K) and beyond; use 16:9 sizes (1920x1080, 2560x1440, 3840x2160). Windows larger than the desktop are allowed.
See ResolutionWidth. 768 = the arcade resolution.

Upscale (recommended): the game runs at its native 1360x768 and the picture is scaled to ResolutionWidth x ResolutionHeight; all 2D elements stay where they belong. Game: the old behaviour, the game's own resolution code runs at that size (above 1360x768 some menus, story talk boxes and ticker clips are misplaced).

3D scene resolution when the output is above 1360x768 (Upscale). Auto: at least the output size (1:1 sharp 3D). Stock: the renderer.ini of the game (ID6 / ID7 962x768, ID8 1443x1152). 1.5x / 2x: that multiple of the output (supersampling, more GPU load).

Initial D starts online by default: at every start TeknoParrot checks the online server, and with this PC registered (Account page) you get nationwide matchmaking, events and rankings. Without registration, or when the server cannot be reached, the game starts offline within seconds. Basic: nothing to set. Advanced: online server, LAN group and peers, seat, cabinet serial, the cabinet's EEPROM network record. Initial D 6 version 1.2 has no online play: it keeps TeknoParrot Online, and its LAN pair now finds the other cabinet by itself (LAN group below) - the three old pair addresses are still there for a 1.2 cabinet that has to be linked by hand.
Initial D 6 Double Ace always uses Auto; the 1.2 build retains its legacy LAN and TPO behaviour. Online when the server answers and this PC is registered; otherwise offline or LAN.

Advanced. The cabinet's own network record in the game's EEPROM (what the game's test menu shows). Online and LAN play use the Windows network of the adapter above, not these values. Leave them as they are unless a test menu needs a fixed address.
Advanced. The cabinet's address in the game's EEPROM network record (when Dhcp is off). Not used for online or LAN play.
Advanced. The subnet mask in the game's EEPROM network record (when Dhcp is off). Not used for online or LAN play.
Advanced. The gateway in the game's EEPROM network record (when Dhcp is off). Not used for online or LAN play.
Advanced. The first DNS server in the game's EEPROM network record (when Dhcp is off). Not used for online or LAN play.
Advanced. The second DNS server in the game's EEPROM network record (when Dhcp is off). Not used for online or LAN play.

Advanced. Initial D 6 version 1.2 only (and the old network mode): the broadcast address its LAN pair link sends the cabinet hellos to - normally the .255 of your network. Version AA does not use it: it links automatically (LAN group above).

Advanced. Initial D 6 version 1.2 only (and the old network mode): the address of cabinet 1 of the pair. Leave it alone unless the other cabinet cannot be found automatically. Version AA does not use it.

Advanced. Initial D 6 version 1.2 only (and the old network mode): the address of cabinet 2 of the pair. Leave it alone unless the other cabinet cannot be found automatically. Version AA does not use it.

Dummy = the game's own dummy ALL.Net (no ALL.Net authentication; the cabinet uses a local dummy store). Real = authenticate against the server's ALL.Net (store name / region come from the server); needs a real network adapter address and DongleRegion / PcbRegion JAPAN. Online play only.

Advanced. LAN group of this cabinet. Empty: TeknoParrot links with the other TeknoParrot PCs of your network after you confirm the link once. A name (the same on every cabinet of one store) separates stores that share a network, counts as the confirmation, and allows LAN play on a network Windows marks as Public. Only PCs with the same group and the same game link.

Advanced. Extra addresses to look for, separated by commas. Normally empty: TeknoParrot finds the other PCs by itself. Needed on networks that do not pass broadcasts (Tailscale and similar), and for a PC on another subnet.
Advanced. The name the other PCs show for this one. Empty = the Windows computer name. It is the only thing this PC puts on the network before a link.

Advanced. Seat of this cabinet in its store. AUTO (recommended): TeknoParrot assigns the seat itself when it finds another TeknoParrot PC on your network, and SINGLE when it finds none. SINGLE: never seated. A1..D2: a fixed seat (tournaments, cabinets that must keep their place). A seat two PCs claim at once sends the later one to SINGLE.

Advanced. Optional cabinet id. Empty = a stable id generated from this PC. Set it only when two PCs would otherwise get the same id (cloned or imaged installs). Online play only. A registered PC uses its Online ID instead on the official server.

Hidden: managed on the Account page (Initial D Online). Your Initial D Online PCB ID (AALG-...), filled in by TeknoParrotUI from your teknoparrot.com account. Used only for online play on the official server; offline and LAN play ignore it. One PC per account.

Hidden: managed on the Account page (Initial D Online). The secret that belongs to OnlineID (43 characters). Keep it private: it lets anyone play as you. Used only for online play on the official server.
Debug: log server box packets, store DB commands and more to TeknoParrot\id6online.log in the game folder.
Debug: log the game's network state (init sequence, store link, DB / match alive, ALL.Net) once per second to TeknoParrot\id6online.log.

Online only: show the opponent's car where it really is, predicted from each packet's age (100-300 ms internet latency: position error p95 about 1.5-2.5 m). Also stops the stock game's opponent running hundreds of meters ahead of a slower or crashed car, and during the first 12 % of the course.
Online only: send your car state every N frames. 1 = 60 Hz (recommended with LagComp, about 8.4 kB/s), 0 = the game's own rate (30 Hz).
Text chat with your rival in online matches (F2 type, Enter send, Esc close, Ctrl+1..4 quick phrases, /mute). Goes through the TeknoParrot server; nothing is stored.
Voice chat in online matches, through the server you play on (not stored, not recorded). talk uses your microphone (a headset is advised; no echo cancelling); F3: talk + listen -> listen only -> off.
Optional push-to-talk key; empty = voice activation.
